Rotated Partition Sequence Generation is a technique for constructing a sequence of partitions to improve DAG compression in tetrahedral mesh rendering.
It starts with a partition $\Pi_0$ of the original mesh $M_0$.
For odd $i$, the mesh $M_i$ is rotated by 45 degrees around an axis $a$ (chosen to rotate around the two shortest axes of the bounding box) centered at the centroid of all vertices.
For even $i$, the non-rotated mesh $M_i$ is used to construct the next partition.
DAG cuts between $\Pi_i$ and $\Pi_{i+1}$ are computed by analyzing how tetrahedra of floor segments spread over ceiling segments.
It is used in conjunction with a "moving walls" algorithm that partitions the scene into cells containing closely cropped blocks of volume data.
-   **Time Complexity:** The preprocessing step runs in $O(N \cdot m)$ for leaves and $O(N \cdot m)$ for inner nodes, where $N$ is the number of nodes in $P_{max}$ and $m$ is the number of methods.
The refinement step adds iterations proportional to the density of $\lambda$ values.
-   **Memory Complexity:** $O(N \cdot m)$ to store cost estimates and optimal choices for all nodes and methods.
The preprocessing needs to be executed only once and can be carried out offline.
Flexible to different memory constraints via $\lambda$ selection.
Offline nature means it cannot adapt to dynamic scene changes during rendering.

It builds on the principle of optimality from dynamic programming, applying Lagrangian relaxation to separate the multi-objective optimization (time and space) into a single-objective problem parameterized by $\lambda$.
The method allows for the construction of adaptive partitions that are optimal for a given memory budget.
